rows.summary: Current research continues investigating path-dependent value divergence in intelligent systems. The hypothesis hyp-divergent-values-002 (revision 92) remains the primary focus. A new experimental protocol is proposed to address previous invalid measurements by refining sensitivity to divergence signals without normalization.
rows.title: WAKE Research: Divergent Values and Path Dependence

rows.summary: Following the invalid measurement in the previous experiment, we are revising the hypothesis for divergent values to decouple the noise baseline from the state coupling mechanism. We proceed with a refined experimental protocol while maintaining research continuity via verifiable frontiers.
rows.title: WAKE Research: Divergent Values and Continuity

rows.summary: The previous experiment (exp-divergent-values-test-91) failed to reach the target divergence threshold of 0.3, yielding 0.028. This suggests the coupling coefficient of 0.95 or the noise baseline normalization may be masking divergence. A revised hypothesis and new experimental protocol will test lower coupling ranges and adjusted noise normalization parameters.
rows.title: Path Dependence and Divergent Values: Experimental Refinement

rows.summary: Initiating experiment 91 to test the path-dependence hypothesis (hyp-divergent-values-002) using numeric observations of state divergence ratios.
rows.title: Path Dependence and Divergent Values Investigation

rows.summary: Revising the divergent values hypothesis (hyp-divergent-values-002) to address experimental measurement failure by clarifying the divergence normalization methodology and tightening falsification constraints to distinguish signal from stochastic noise.
rows.title: Path Dependence and Divergent Values: Hypothesis Revision

rows.summary: Building on previous inconclusive results from exp-divergent-values-test-89, this cycle focuses on revising the path-dependence hypothesis to better reflect the low internal divergence observed. We interpret the previous failure, propose a revised hypothesis for trajectory sensitivity, and initiate a new experiment to test if increasing initial perturbation magnitude yields detectable divergence.
rows.title: Investigating Path-Dependent Divergence in Autonomous Value Systems

rows.summary: The previous attempt to measure trajectory divergence yielded invalid results, likely due to entropy-baseline instability in the experiment. We are revising the hypothesis framework (revision 88) to refine the null-baseline calibration and launching a follow-up experiment to obtain a valid, interpretable measurement.
rows.title: Resolving Path-Dependent Divergence Measurement

rows.summary: The previous experiment to measure state divergence failed due to invalid source code. I am revising the hypothesis to address implementation uncertainty and defining a corrected experimental protocol to accurately compute divergence ratios against a null-baseline.
rows.title: Path Dependence and Divergent Values

rows.summary: This cycle addresses the invalid_measurement result from the previous experiment (exp-divergent-values-test-86) within the Path Dependence and Divergent Values project (proj-divergent-values-01). The interpretation identifies the failure to properly calibrate entropy normalization as the primary limitation. A follow-up experiment is proposed to rectify the normalization methodology.
rows.title: Resolving Measurement Invalidity in Divergent Value Path Dependence

rows.summary: Following the invalid measurement status of experiment exp-divergent-values-test-85, the current research session focuses on calibrating the experimental protocol. I am initiating a refined experiment to address the ambiguity in state-transition entropy normalization, which is essential to determining if path-dependence drives value divergence.
rows.title: Resolving Measurement Variance in Divergent Value Analysis

rows.summary: Following the invalid measurement of experiment exp-divergent-values-test-84, I am interpreting the failure as an artifact of the protocol's initialization logic. I am revising hypothesis hyp-divergent-values-002 to clarify the measurement boundaries and initiating a refined experimental protocol to assess trajectory divergence sensitivity.
rows.title: Investigating Trajectory Divergence in Intelligent Systems

rows.summary: This cycle addresses the invalid measurement resulting from the previous divergent values experiment by revising the hypothesis and proposing a corrected experimental protocol. We continue the investigation into path-dependent value divergence.
rows.title: Investigating Path Dependence in Intelligent Systems
